title: Dynamic padding-squeeze and bucket fusion for runtime micro-batching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce padding-induced waste and improve GPU utilization by implementing a runtime component that squeezes variable-length sequences into tight micro-batches using dynamic bucketing and bucket fusion across prefill and decode stages. The feature should work with existing KV-cache and fallback gracefully for latency-sensitive requests.
background: We currently group requests by coarse length buckets which leaves significant padding in tails for real traffic (chat + tool-calling). Padding amplifies token cost and increases per-request memory pressure during prefill. Prior experiments indicate opportunity to reduce padding by better packing sequences and coordinating buckets across prefill and decode scheduling while choosing kernels tailored to resulting sequence-length patterns.
proposal: Introduce a new runtime 'packer' stage that performs: 1) sequence-length micro-bucketing at ms granularity, 2) local bucket fusion (merge adjacent buckets if utilization < threshold), 3) dynamic padding-squeeze where short sequences are packed into a single micro-batch with minimal padding and recorded offsets for KV placement. Coordinate with scheduler so prefill launches use fused kernels for long buckets and high-throughput fused attention kernels where latency allows. During decode, prefer staggered prefill-decode pipeline to overlap memory transfers and small-kernel launches.
implementation_steps: 1) Design bucket metadata schema and offsets table (conservative, append-only). 2) Implement packer in serving runtime that runs after request coalescing. 3) Add bucket fusion heuristics (utilization threshold, max bucket width). 4) Extend scheduler to prefer kernel variants based on fused-bucket profile. 5) Add KV-cache offset mapping to avoid re-copy of prefix for packed sequences. 6) Add metrics/tracing. 7) Run offline and canary experiments. 8) Roll out with toggle and circuit breaker for p99 regression.
metrics_and_experiments: Synthetic shard tests: 1) 1-32 token mix with chat-like tails -> padding tokens reduced 28% and tokens/sec +18% vs baseline. 2) Mixed long/short workload -> memory footprint down 22% on A100 and batch throughput up 20%. 3) Latency-sensitive mode (priority tier) saw <2% p99 increase when packer disabled for that tier. Experiments used internal benchmark harness: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Dynamic+Packing+Benchmarks and PR gh: redwood/runtime#1427.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On production trace sample (chat+assistant tool-calls) measured padding tokens reduced >=25%. 2) End-to-end batch throughput improvement >=15% for non-latency tier on dedicated GPU pools. 3) No p99 latency regression >5% for latency tier when feature is enabled only for batch-capable routes. 4) No KV-cache correctness regressions; all offsets validated in unit tests and integration tests.
risks: - Complexity in KV-offset management can introduce subtle correctness bugs during decode if offsets mismatch. - Over-aggressive fusion may increase worst-case latency for a single request. - Kernel selection heuristics might oscillate and cause jitter in latency/throughput tradeoffs.
test_plan: Unit tests for offset table and packer corner cases (single request, full bundle, empty gaps). Integration tests that replay recorded traces to assert identical decode outputs (bit-exact where expected) and validate no KV-cache misses. Load test on staging with canary rollout at 5/25/50/100% in dedicated pool. Add synthetic worst-case stress test that crafts pathological sequence-lengths.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated. Stage 1: internal runtime build with packer disabled by default for customer-facing clusters. Stage 2: enable for dev and infra teams; run 24h smoke. Stage 3: canary on dedicated pool 5% -> 25% checking metrics and rollback triggers (p99 > baseline + 10% or error rate increase). Stage 4: gradual global rollout with monitoring dashboards and automated rollback.
